course_name_original: German B2 course - compulsory course of 135 hours for students of FIRST-CYCLE studies - semester 3/3
course_name_en: German B2 course - compulsory course of 135 hours for first-cycle students - semester 3/3
prerequisites: German language knowledge at least at A-2 level.

learning_outcomes.text: Can write understandable informative and argumentative texts on general and industry topics, conduct correspondence typical for the work environment, and independently use didactic materials.
Can clearly present conclusions and opinions on general, academic, and professional topics in written and oral form.
Understands longer, even complex written and oral statements, e.g., lectures and presentations, provided they concern industry issues and current affairs, and can interpret the obtained information.

Can use grammatical structures, phraseology, and vocabulary that allow understanding general texts describing contemporary economic and social phenomena, academic and industry-specific texts, and allow for fairly fluent and spontaneous communication in academic and professional environments.
Can prepare an oral presentation on academic and industry topics and participate in discussions quite fluently and spontaneously, also in a professional environment.

syllabus_topics: Grammatical issues: Präteritum tense, Plusquamperfekt tense, Futur I tense, Subordinate clauses with weil, dass, obwohl, trotzdem, Temporal clauses with als, wenn, während, nachdem, seit, sobald, bis, bevor, solange, Adjective declension – Adjektivdeklination, Relative clauses - Relativsätze, Compound conjunctions: je ... desto ..., nicht ... sondern ..., nicht nur ... sondern auch, Weder .... noch, entweder .... oder, Passive voice - Passiv, Passive voice with modal verbs, Verb government – Verben mit Präpositionen, Subjunctive mood: Konjunktiv Präteritum und Plusquamperfekt, Irreal conditional sentences – Irreale Konditionalsätze, Conjunctions: “darum, deshalb, deswegen”, Infinitive with “zu” and without “zu” - Infinitiv mit und ohne zu, Modal particles: denn, doch, ja, eigentlich, mal, Preposition wegen, Participles: Partizip I und II, Verb “lassen”, Infinitive constructions: Infinitivkonstruktionen: um..zu, ohne…zu, anstatt…zu, Conjunctions: Konjuktionen: damit, ohne dass, anstatt dass, Adverbial clause of manner: Modalsatz indem, dadurch dass, Temporal adverbs, Negation words, Multi-part conjunctions: zwar……..aber, einerseits……… andererseits

Topics and Vocabulary: Communication media - Kommunikationsmedien, Computer und Internet, Holidays and celebrations - Feste und Feiertage, Travel- Reisen, Living - Wohnen, Education in Germany and Poland - Schulen in Deutschland und in Polen, Climate and environment, weather, environmental pollution - Klima und Umwelt: Wetter, Umweltprobleme, Professional life - Berufsleben, berufliche Ziele, Cultural events - Musik, Veranstaltungen, Lifelong learning - Lebenslanges Lernen, Learning foreign languages - Fremdsprachenlernen, Applying for a job – Bewerbung, Suche nach der Arbeit, Finance, banking, conducting business calls - Fit für Finanzen, Fit am Telefon, Fit für die Firma, Studies, description of the faculty and nature of studies, Industry-specific vocabulary.

Language functions and other skills: Conducting discussions – eine Diskussion führen, Commenting on information - Informationen kommentieren, Discussing photos and memories - Über Fotos und Erinnerungen sprechen, Discussing everyday life situations - Über Alltagsprobleme sprechen, Giving advice – Ratschläge geben, Expressing wishes – Wünsche ausdrücken, Forecasting - Prognosen machen, Stating reasons - Gründe nennen, Naming conditions and consequences -Bedingungen und Konsequenzen nennen, Conflict resolution, reacting in conflict situations-Konflikte erkennen, verstehen und lösen, Discussing rules of conduct and gestures -Über Verhaltensregeln und Gesten sprechen, Conducting short conversations with casually met people (Smalltalksituationen), Proposing and arguing, presenting one's own position, constructively criticizing, Preparing and conducting a job interview, Filling out forms, Editing various types of texts: emails and private and official letters, e.g., cover letter, CV, letters to the editor as a reaction to a read article, Listening comprehension of interviews, general conversations, as well as popular science statements, Reading comprehension of popular science written texts, Conducting a professional presentation related to the field of study.
assessment_rules: The condition for obtaining credit is receiving a positive grade from all colloquia conducted during the semester. In case of a negative grade, the student has the right to improve the grade according to the following rules: improving a negative grade obtained in the first attempt results in cancelling the negative grade and replacing it with a positive grade which will count towards the average; improving a grade obtained in the second attempt results in entering the average of the two grades obtained into the record sheet, where the average partial grade for passing the test cannot be less than 3.0. An unjustified absence from a test results in forfeiture of the attempt, and each student has the right to two retake colloquia, which can take place at intervals of not less than 2 days. The final grade for the language course is determined as the arithmetic average of all grades obtained by the student from the credits of individual semesters and the foreign language exam. The student must attend all classes of their language group; if absent due to illness, a medical certificate must be provided no later than 14 days after the excused absence. For unjustified absence, the student should contact the instructor to arrange individual make-up methods within 14 days from the date of absence; unjustified absence from two classes does not require make-up. If the number of unjustified absences exceeds 7, the instructor should refuse to credit the semester, even if some of them were previously made up. The student is obliged to have a language textbook and complete homework assignments; failure to have the required materials (textbook, homework) results in an annotation of 'unprepared' in the record sheet. The instructor has the right to refuse to credit a student who was unprepared for more than 1/2 of the classes, even if they passed all colloquia. Additional grades are awarded for activity in class, optional homework, presentations, and other activities for their class group. The condition for admission to the exam is passing the compulsory language course semesters.
